assets.strategy_rationale: The spec explicitly states 'do not generate any image assets, use solid colours only', which aligns with a procedural asset strategy.

architecture.test_input_example: Press RIGHT, then DOWN several times until piece locks. Repeat until a row clears. Press UP to rotate. Press R to restart. Press ESC to quit.

decisions.reason: Tetris is conventionally a single-player game unless multiplayer is explicitly mentioned, and the spec does not mention multiple players.

A 10x20 grid with 20x20 pixel blocks would be 200x400. Doubling this for better visibility and adding space for score display results in 400x600, which is a common and sensible resolution for simple 2D games.
60 FPS is a standard frame rate for smooth real-time games and provides a good balance between responsiveness and performance for a simple game like Tetris.

decisions.choice: Each of the four piece shapes (square, line, L-shape, T-shape) will be assigned a distinct, solid color (e.g., yellow, cyan, orange, magenta).
decisions.reason: The spec requires 'one colour per piece shape' and 'use solid colours only'. Specific colors are chosen to be visually distinct.
This size makes the 10x20 grid fit well within the chosen 400x600 resolution (200x400 for the grid itself, leaving space for score/UI).

decisions.choice: The piece will fall one row every 500 milliseconds (0.5 seconds).
decisions.reason: This provides a reasonable starting difficulty for the 'constant rate' falling, allowing players time to react without being too slow.

decisions.choice: Pieces will spawn horizontally centered at the top of the grid, with their top-most block at row 0.
decisions.reason: The spec states 'spawns at the top-middle of the grid'. This interpretation ensures pieces are visible and centered.

decisions.choice: The score will be displayed in the top-right corner of the window, with a small margin from the edge.
decisions.reason: The spec requires 'Show the current score in the top-right corner'. A small margin ensures it's readable and not flush with the window edge.

decisions.choice: The 'GAME OVER' message and final score will be displayed centrally on the screen.
decisions.reason: This is a common and clear way to present game over information in simple games.
